subject: computer-science
title: Data & Binary: Text & Images
welcome_lead: How does a computer store letters, photos and emojis? In bits!
meta_desc: KS3 binary: ASCII, pixels, resolution, colour depth.
final_note: Text is numbers, images are grids of numbers — everything is data.

concepts.def: A code that maps characters to numbers.
A bigger code that covers many languages.
A single dot of colour in an image.
Number of pixels across and down.
How many bits store the colour of one pixel.
An image stored as a grid of pixels.

walkthroughs.body_html: In ASCII, the letter A is 65, B is 66, and so on. Each character fits in one byte. Modern computers use Unicode to cover thousands of symbols.
A photo is a grid of tiny squares called pixels. Each pixel holds a colour as numbers (often red, green, blue). More pixels = sharper image but bigger file.
1 bit per pixel gives 2 colours (black and white). 8 bits gives 256 colours. 24 bits gives millions — enough for any photo.
